bug_report: The nightly export to the ERP is corrupting rows - any product description containing a comma spills into the next column and shifts everything after it. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix the export so field values arrive in the ERP intact, without breaking existing behaviour.

conversations.text: The ERP import mangled our part numbers again — "00042" came in as "42" and the SKU lookups all broke.
The importer is coercing digit fields to numbers. I'll switch the export to quote every field with standard CSV quotes — quoted values should be read as text.
We tried exactly that last year — the ERP still coerces a quoted digit string to a number and strips the zeros. Ordinary quoting doesn't stop it.
Then what form does the ERP actually keep verbatim?
Excel-style text formulas. A digit-only value with a leading zero has to be written as ="00042" — that's the only thing its parser imports byte-for-byte.
Understood. Should I write every field in that formula form, to be safe?

No — only the leading-zero digit strings. Everything else is normal CSV with minimal quoting: quote a field only if it contains a comma, a quote, or a newline, and double any embedded quotes. And rows must end with \r\n — the ERP parser rejects bare \n line endings.

Final: digit-strings with a leading zero are written as ="..."; all other fields use minimal quoting with doubled embedded quotes; comma delimiter; CRLF row endings. Round-trip through the ERP preserves every value exactly.

policy: leading-zero digit strings written as ="..." text form; minimal quoting; CRLF
non_guessable: the ="..." text form + CRLF, not QUOTE_ALL which passes the repro
